title: Eight months with Art Blakey, the Keystone Corner and a Coltrane book
summary: Branford spent eight months in Blakey's band; they trade remarks about the Keystone Corner and a book on John Coltrane.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, let’s go back to your development as a saxophonist. So, you’re in Art Blakey’s…. How long were you in Art Blakey’s band?
And I remember seeing you at the Keystone Corner, probably eighty-one, eighty-two, no, eighty-two.
That was fun. That was fun. I loved that place.
So…. You loved that place? Oh, yeah, the Keystone Corner, did you see the book?
Kathy Sloane, she’s got a book out.
Yeah, beautiful. You’ll love it. You know that book on Trane. We’ll talk about that off- tape.
There’s a recent book by Oxford University Press called “Coltrane and….” What is it called? I contributed one chapter, but it’s called John Coltrane and Black America’s Quest for Freedom.
It’s all-black, all-black contributors. Scholars and musicians. You know Leonard Brown.
He’s up at Northeastern. Anyway, he’s held the Coltrane festival. He’s the editor. If you don’t have a copy, I’ll get you a copy.
